title: I Built a Lead-Qualification AI Agent (Before a Human Follows Up)
content:
Most lead follow-ups are either too slow
or too pushy.
So I built an AI agent that QUALIFIES a
LEAD FIRST,
and only then waits for a human to follow up.

This is Project 2 in my build-in-public
week on AI agents and automations.
I work with CRMs a lot, including HubSpot
on client work,
so I wanted an agent that scores and sorts leads
WITHOUT sending a single outbound message
on its own.
Stay till the end, because the KILL SWITCH
is the part most people skip.

Step 1. Write hot, warm and cold criteria
in PLAIN ENGLISH.
Not vibes. Not "feels promising."
Hot might mean: asked for a demo, named a
budget, and has a clear use case.
Warm might mean: filled the form, but no
budget yet.
Cold might mean: student email, no
company, or a one-word message.
If you cannot write the rules, the agent
cannot follow them.

Step 2. Decide what the agent can READ
versus what it must NEVER invent.
It can read form fields and CRM fields
that already exist.
Name, company, role, message, source, past
emails if they are in the CRM.
It must NEVER invent a budget, a timeline,
or a pain point that was not written down.
That one rule alone stops a lot of bad AI
sales behaviour.

Step 3. The agent SCORES the lead and
DRAFTS a reply.
It does not send.
Imagine a small agency gets 40 form leads a day.
Someone used to open each one, decide if
it is real, and copy it into a sheet.
Say the agent tags each lead hot, warm or cold,
writes a short reason, and drafts a
follow-up in a note.
A human still presses send. That is the
whole point.

Step 4. Put a HUMAN APPROVAL GATE before
any outbound message.
This is the same pattern businesses are
adopting with workflow tools.
AWS just made Step Functions available as
AI agent tools through Bedrock AgentCore
Gateway,
so irreversible steps like refunds or
sends stay in a fixed order the model
cannot improvise.
Your lead agent should work the same way.
Qualify and draft. Then wait.

Step 5. Log every decision for a weekly review.
Score, reason, draft, and whether a human
approved or changed it.
Step 6. Add a KILL SWITCH.
Disable send tools completely until you
trust the drafts for 2 weeks.
If the agent cannot send, it cannot spam
your list.

Here's my take.
A lead-qualification agent is only useful
if it makes the human faster,
not if it replaces judgment on day 1.
Start with score plus draft. Keep the
human on the send button.
Then tighten the criteria every week from the log.
